en: Preface to the *Painful Exhortation to Pure Practice* (*Jingye tongce*) The *Painful Exhortation to Pure Practice* was composed by the Great Master Kongling of Zhenyang, whose name was Zhao Ying and whose style name was Guixi.

He profoundly rejoiced in the Dharma and greatly praised the Buddha’s grace; moreover, he repeatedly expounded upon his devotion to the Great Master who dwells in the West. I have appended this preface here.
This exhortation on the virtue of compassion can truly serve as a self-reproach and a reproach for others.
Those who wish to swiftly accomplish pure karma must rely upon this; its contribution to the Pure Land is by no means trivial.

My inclusion of this among those works essential for seeking rebirth in the Pure Land is due to the personal instruction of Master Yuanlian. Having seen this book of earnest admonition, I find it most timely.

This work will surely be widely disseminated in the world. Fearing that those who love learning might find it too concise, I have once again poured forth my heart’s blood to compile this book as an aid to it.
Its words are earnest and its vows are profoundly sincere; I am ashamed of my own ignorance and have no words with which to praise it.
I can only kneel before the Buddha and reverently burn forty-eight incense sticks from my arm as an offering.
While making offerings to Amitābha Buddha, he made this vow: "By what past merit have I now encountered this teacher in this life?
Having heard these subtle and wondrous words, I am certain that the Lotus Pond may be hoped for. Therefore, I burn my arm as incense to make offerings to Amitābha Buddha;
I vow that until the end of the future, I shall always follow such exhortations. This book is also titled *A Painful Exhortation to Pure Practice*; it can truly be called [such].

This is the greatest among all poignant strategies. There was a lay follower from Xidao named Jingyou, who conceived the aspiration to sponsor the carving [of these texts] in order to cultivate pure causes.
He vowed that all who see or hear them would give rise to faith, vows, and practice, so that throughout this present physical existence, they might together be reborn in the Pure Land.
Written in the third year of the Guangxu era, during the first month of summer, by the practitioner of Pure Land, Xin Yong, with prostrations at Fayuan Hermitage in Shanyin.
Appended to the *Painful Exhortation for Pure Land Practitioners*.
The *Litanies and Visualization Ritual for the Amitābha Sūtra* was composed by the Great Master [Yunqi] Jian, who respectfully followed the *Amitābha Practice Ritual* described by Master Jianzhu.
By condensing the extensive into the concise, the meaning of the sūtra is rendered even more manifest; with diligent effort and profound contemplation, it is truly marvelous and ultimate.
Consequently, those practitioners under his guidance all praised it as excellent, for the present single thought is inherently endowed with vastness.
With this mind, one universally pays homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem of the ten directions and the three periods of time.

Entrusting oneself to the eternally abiding Triple Gem of the ten directions and the three periods of time, one suddenly manifests the vast and great mind inherently possessed within the present single thought-moment.

This is what is meant by: being oneself and yet others; being principle and yet phenomena; being true emptiness and wondrous existence; and the cause encompassing the ocean of fruition, while the fruition penetrates to the source of the cause. It is...

Throughout the ten ages of past and present, beginning and end do not depart from the present moment; within the ocean of lands as numerous as motes of dust, self and other are not separated by even a hair’s breadth.
It is for this reason that by holding a single scroll of the small *Amitābha Sūtra*, one is protected and remembered by all Buddhas of the ten directions and three periods of time.
Thus, the *Yaojie* (Essential Explanation) says: "The profound treasury of the *Avataṃsaka* and the secret..."
The marrow of all Buddhas’ essential teachings and the compass for the myriad practices of Bodhisattvas—none of these transcend this.
One should know that this ritual is the essential method for the perfect purification of the three karmas. The uttering of sound is the purification of the karma of speech.
Prostrating is the purification of the physical karma (*kāyakarma*). Contemplating the scriptural text in silence is the purification of the mental karma (*manaskarma*).
Furthermore, adding prostration on the knees while chanting aloud is the ultimate method for purifying both body and speech.

If one practices with such earnestness and utmost sincerity, how could the Buddhas of the ten directions—Amitābha and Śākyamuni—not certainly and swiftly bestow their protection, so that at the moment of death, [one’s rebirth] is certain?
One will attain rebirth; not only is rebirth certain, but one shall also surely behold the Buddha at an early date.
Those who wish to enter the Sahā world swiftly to universally deliver all sentient beings must likewise rely upon this.

Such merits are constantly praised without ceasing by the Buddhas of the ten directions with their broad and long tongues—how could they ever be fully exhausted? I pray that future practitioners of pure karma will not fail to exert themselves to the utmost.
We practiced it together. All that precedes was personally proclaimed by the Master; I have merely recorded it as I followed his instructions.

At this time, in the summer of the third year of the Guangxu era, the junior student Xinyong respectfully wrote this at Baen Hermitage, following the *Buddha-spoken Sutra of Amitābha* and its ritual for veneration and visualization.
The Disciple of the Western Śākyamuni, Gu Kunzun, has briefly compiled this for practitioners.
Whenever performing ritual visualization, first kneel before the Buddha and burn incense; then, with palms joined, say:

May these clouds of incense smoke pervade the worlds of the ten directions, making offerings to all Buddhas and this Dharma that is difficult for the world to believe, as well as to all superior and virtuous persons.
May they universally perfume all sentient beings, causing them all to resolve upon Bodhicitta. (Then rise and prostrate to the Buddha.)

With single-minded devotion, I prostrate and pay homage. To the World-Honored One, Śākyamuni Buddha, our Original Teacher, who in this Sahā world of the five turbidities and evil age preaches the Dharma that is difficult to believe—[prostrate and silently contemplate one passage from the sutra, beginning with: "Śāriputra, as I now praise the inconceivable merit of the Buddhas," down to "this is most difficult."

With single-minded devotion, prostrate in homage. Throughout the worlds of the ten directions, [the Buddhas] extend their broad and long tongues to exhort and praise the West—the Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River (from "Śāriputra, as I now praise the inconceivable merit and benefits of Amitābha Buddha" down to "the Sūtra Protected and Mindfully Kept by All Buddhas Above").
With single-minded devotion, pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, whose light and lifespan are immeasurable, who universally gathers all sentient beings.
(Śāriputra, what do you think? For what reason is that Buddha named Amitābha? [From here down to "ten kalpas have now passed"].)
With single-minded devotion, prostrate in homage. In the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, by upholding the Name, one is guided at the moment of death by Amitābha Buddha.
(Śāriputra, it is not by means of few roots of goodness... down to: one should resolve to be born in that land.)
With single-minded devotion, pay homage. To the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, I now make this vow:
may all beings be enabled to be reborn there. Amitābha Buddha. (Śāriputra, if there be anyone who has already made the vow... down to "be born in that land.")

With single-minded devotion, pay homage and extol the *Sūtra on the Merit of Inconceivable Virtues, Protected and Mindfully Sustained by All Buddhas*, as well as all the Honored Dharmas of the ten directions and the three periods of time. (Śāriputra, what do you think? For what reason is it called... [and so forth, down to] ...the teachings spoken by all Buddhas.)

With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the World of Ultimate Bliss in the western quarter, to Avalokiteśvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, and all the noble and virtuous ones, as well as the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas in the pure great ocean.
(Furthermore, Śāriputra, that Buddha has immeasurable and boundless śrāvaka disciples, down to those gathered together in one place.)

With single-minded devotion, prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, beneath the trees where the spiritual birds dwell, who maintain right mindfulness upon hearing their voices.
(Furthermore, Śāriputra, that land always possesses various wondrous and multicolored birds, down to the phrase: "having thus accomplished such majestic adornments of merit.")

With single-minded devotion, prostrate in homage. Upon the golden ground of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, one offers abundant flowers as an offering to the Buddha and the various Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
(Furthermore, Śāriputra, in that buddha-land, celestial music constantly plays, down to the point where it says "adorned with merit.")
With single-minded devotion, pay homage to the various Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas within the precious pavilions in the lotus ponds of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
(Furthermore, Śāriputra, in the land of Ultimate Bliss there are ponds made of the seven treasures, down to the description of their meritorious adornments.)

With single-minded devotion, pay homage to the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, where there is no suffering whatsoever, but only the experience of all manner of joys, and where all Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas [reside].
(At that time the Buddha addressed the Elder... down to: "For this reason, that land is called Ultimate Bliss.")
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to Mañjuśrī, Maitreya, and all the great Bodhisattvas; to Śāriputra and all the great Āryas;
and to all the holy multitudes of the ten directions and the three periods of time. (Thus have I heard... down to "...and the vast assembly of immeasurable devas.")
Having completed the ritual visualization, kneel and recite one scroll of the *Amitābha Sūtra* and the *Wǎngshēng Zhòu* (Dharani for Rebirth) three times.
Then offer this praise: "Amitābha Buddha’s body is golden in color; His marks and signs and radiant light are peerless. The white tuft of hair between his brows curls like five Mount Sumerus;
His deep blue eyes are as clear as the four great oceans. Within his light, countless billions of transformation Buddhas appear, And hosts of transformed Bodhisattvas likewise..."
Boundless. Through forty-eight vows, he delivers sentient beings, causing those of all nine grades to ascend to the other shore.

Homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, the Greatly Compassionate and Greatly Merciful One. (Recite the name of the Buddha as many times as your strength permits, then cease.)
Namo Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Namo Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva. Namo to the assembly of Bodhisattvas of the Pure Great Ocean (recite each ten times).
Having completed the recitation, dedicate the merit and make this vow:
The disciple calls upon the name of Amitābha, The Buddha of True Merit;
I pray that you, out of compassion, will grant your acceptance, And bear witness to my repentance and my vows.
All the evil karma I have created in the past Arises entirely from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion.
I now repent of everything arising from my body, speech, and mind. May I,
at the time when my life is about to end, Have all obstacles completely eliminated,
And behold that Buddha Amitābha face-to-face, Thereby attaining rebirth in the Land of Peace and Bliss.

All the roots of goodness I have now cultivated, I dedicate them all entirely, universally aspiring that all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm may together be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
I take refuge in the Buddha; may all sentient beings realize the Great Way and give rise to the unsurpassed mind.
Taking refuge in the Dharma, may all beings enter deeply into the treasury of the sūtras, their wisdom as vast as the ocean.
Taking refuge in the Saṃgha, may all beings lead great assemblies, free from all obstacles.

Homage to the Noble Assembly. (The Sūtra states: "There are many Bodhisattvas who wish to hear this sūtra but are unable to do so. If there are sentient beings who hear this sūtra, they shall never regress from the Unsurpassed Way. Therefore, one should single-mindedly believe, accept, uphold, recite, explain, and practice it.

Regarding the ritual for prostration and visualization: this is based on what appears in the Sūtra; it is the most essential of essentials and the most urgent of urgencies. As for how many times one wishes to prostrate each day, let it be according to one's own capacity; however, the two periods of morning and evening must by no means be omitted).
A Simple Method for Dedication at the Time of Sleep (The Elder Ānanda Should Follow This Ritual for Taking Refuge in the West):
At the time of sleep, kneel before the Buddha with palms joined. With utmost sincerity and all one's strength, recite:
*Namo Amitābha Buddha* (ten breaths) *Namo Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva* *Namo Mahā...*
Śrī-Ābhāsvara Bodhisattva. *Namo* to the assembly of pure great ocean-like Bodhisattvas (ten recitations each).

The vow is made as follows: "I, disciple [Name], am currently an ordinary being in the cycle of birth and death. My karmic obstacles are profound and heavy; I transmigrate through the six realms, and my suffering is beyond description.
Now, having encountered a spiritual friend, I have been able to hear the name of Amitābha Buddha and the merits of his original vows. With single-minded devotion, I shall recite it."
I pray for rebirth in that land. May the Buddha, out of compassion, not forsake me; may he look upon me with pity and grant me his protection.

This disciple, [Name], does not recognize the Buddha’s body, its marks of excellence, or its radiance. I pray that the Buddha will manifest himself so that I may behold him, as well as Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
I have clearly perceived the assembly of bodhisattvas, the pure adornments of that world, and its wondrous marks of radiance.
(Having prostrated three times before the Buddha, I returned to my quarters to rest.)
The Orthodox Lineage of the Lotus School:
The First Patriarch, Great Master Huiyuan of Mount Lu (passed away on the sixth day of the eighth lunar month).
The Second Patriarch, Great Master Shandao of Guangming (birth date of Amitābha not yet determined; offerings should be made on this day).
The Third Patriarch, Grand Master Banzhou Chengyuan (passed away on the nineteenth day of the seventh month);
the Fourth Patriarch, Grand Master Wuhui Fazhao (passed away on the first day of the twelfth month);
the Fifth Patriarch, Grand Master Taiyan Shaokang (passed away on the third day of the tenth month).
The Sixth Patriarch, Great Master Yongming Yijue (passed away on the twenty-sixth day of the second month);
the Seventh Patriarch, Great Master Zhaoking Shengchang (passed away on the twelfth day of the first month);
the Eighth Patriarch, Great Master Yunqi Lianchi (passed away on the second day of the seventh month).
The Ninth Patriarch, Great Master Ouyi Lingfeng (passed away on the twenty-first day of the first month);
The Tenth Patriarch, Great Master Fantian Siqi (passed away on the fourteenth day of the fourth month);
The Eleventh Patriarch, Great Master Chuewu Zifú (passed away on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month).

As for the patriarchs mentioned above, out of compassion for those in the final age who have no means to escape suffering, they exerted their strength to propagate this school and extensively deliver all classes of beings.

How can their compassionate kindness and virtue be adequately discussed? That we, on this day, place our faith in the power of Amitābha’s vows in the Western Land, resolve to cultivate the practice of reciting the Name, and determine to seek birth there, is entirely due to the kindness and virtue of these patriarchs. This is...
Therefore, on the day of one's rebirth in the Pure Land, one should reverently prepare offerings and either respectfully burn incense on one’s arm.
First, one rejoices in having heard the Dharma and holds the Name with ever-increasing earnestness; second, one seeks its hidden empowerment so that rebirth may be achieved even more swiftly.

I pray that all pure friends will join me in this endeavor. On a summer day in the year of Bingzi, the junior student Gukun, facing the various patriarchs, respectfully inscribed this record after burning three incense sticks from his own arm as a mark of prostration.
This is the origin of the earnest exhortation for the practice of Pure Karma.
I, Zhao Ying, am unworthy; my karmic obstructions are deep and heavy, while my roots of goodness are faint and shallow.
Although I have encountered spiritual teachers and gained faith that reciting the Buddha’s name is the supreme dharma, I have yet to grasp the essential method for holding the name.
Consequently, I am constantly shaken by delusive thoughts and doubts, unable to resolve my will. Having heard that Master Xianlou advocated for the Pure Land with all his might, I daily recite—
He recited the name of Amitābha tens of thousands of times; though it was intensely hot or cold, he never slackened even slightly.

He compiled the *Essential Readings for the Lotus School*, the *Direct Path to the West*, the *Self-Admonition for the Pure Land*, the *Divine Pearl of the Pure Land*, the *Ritual for Returning to the West*, as well as the *Diverse Phenomena of Sūtras and Vinaya* and the *Verses on Opening the Mind through Nianfo*.
These works circulated throughout the world, and at that time, those who partook of the milk of the Dharma were not few. [His style was] profound and lucid.
My merit and virtue were meager, and I had not yet been fortunate enough to receive his personal instruction.

In the winter of the Jiawu year, when the Master entered seclusion at Fayuan Hermitage on Mount Shaoyin, I went there to pay my respects and personally rely upon him as his disciple. Under his guidance, I was granted the most essential and vital teachings, which he spoke thus:
"If you can give rise to resolute faith and single-mindedly uphold this one great name, it is simply like an infant falling into water and crying out in urgency."
"Mother, save me! she cried, her voice never ceasing. It was not necessary to observe external forms or eliminate delusions;

naturally, there was a resonance between us as our paths met, and pure karma was easily accomplished. Upon hearing these profound words, I, Yingqin, was moved beyond measure—like a blind man regaining his sight, joy and compassion flowed together.
Not deeming my own learning sufficient, I have勉力 (striven) to compose eight gāthās, along with ten occasional verses, and a sequence of verses following Master Miaoneng’s *Pure Land* [hymns].
These thirty original rhymes for the poems comprise forty-eight drafts in total. I respectfully present them before the Master’s gate.

Grateful for the Master’s great kindness in meticulously revising and correcting them, I have carefully recorded this single compilation as a lifelong admonition for my own improvement—much like a dull horse that only moves forward after being struck by a painful whip.

In the autumn of the Yi-hai year of the Guangxu era, the junior disciple Zhao Yingran of Chenyang, with nine incense sticks bound to his arm, prostrates himself and respectfully records this as a painful exhortation for the Pure Land practice.
The Later Student Zhao Ying compiled this from his own lamentation:

"For ten thousand kalpas I have wandered in saṃsāra, trapped in the river of craving; all is due to the abundance of greedy attachments and deluded passions. This time, I must not fail to seek liberation early."

Liberated, yet fearing that at the moment of death one might cry out "What shall I do?"—skin, hair, flesh, bones, and marrow shall fall away like a mountain; turning back to see the time of delusion, tears flow silently and profusely.
If one does not hear the Dharma for the removal of suffering in this life, how could one know to make vows to transcend the mundane world?
Whenever anger arises, it is like a pack of wild beasts; it is solely because of the self and others that distinctions are made.
From now on, I shall gradually cool the fire of the red furnace, relying entirely upon the merit and transformative power of Amitābha.
I clearly know that wealth and honor are but floating bubbles; I regret how I once sought them with all my might.
My tattered robes and meager soup are now sufficient; thus, I have neither joy nor sorrow.

I rejoice that throughout these years I have recited the Buddha’s name, yet I lament my own blindness and folly. Like an infant crying for its mother, I was unaware of my suffering. How fortunate that the essential school has extended its salvation to me;
for the rest of my life, I shall faithfully accept and remember my enlightened teacher.
I regret from the past my lack of roots of goodness; I mistakenly took delusive thoughts for enemies. Now, fortunately, I have encountered the path within paths;
let the waves of affliction surge as they will.
I have humbly received your boundless grace of salvation; you have untied the knots of my base and inferior self.
Through the combined power of faith, aspiration, and practice, the sails are set for the Land of Bliss, swift as the wind.
Longing to see my compassionate parents, I disregard my own person; morning and evening I pay homage and recite their names, enduring toil and hardship.
I only hope to soon receive news from my homeland, so that when the time comes to return to the Land of Bliss, I may stretch out my arm.
Having by chance attained human form, all things are difficult to retain. Those with discernment joyfully cultivate the direct path.
Fully upholding the six syllables without interruption, one will surely return to the place of succession, forever free from fault.

In a mere instant, the dream of death is realized; how can one afford to indulge in negligence and pursue worldly sentiments? Over the years, I have traveled everywhere seeking the Dharma of horizontal transcendence, yet I have not yet obtained the refined instructions for holding the Name.

Having sought them out, you have already reached the region of Shanyin; how could your close companions and teachers allow this to be in vain? It only requires that you hold the name as if calling for your mother;
there is no need for investigation or penetrating the three barriers.
I realize early that the Dharma of holding the Name is most essential; I deeply regret my past delusions that led me down divergent paths. From this day forth, I shall count the beads of Amitābha;
its boundless merit can all be fully realized.

Drifting and sinking through birth and death for countless years, it was solely due to drowning in attachment that I was ensnared by worldly passions. Now, fortunately, I have obtained the Dharma of holding the Name;
I only pray that I may soon board the vessel of Ultimate Bliss.

Do not worry that karmic offenses cannot be eliminated; with firm and deep faith and aspiration, they will surely be dispelled. By reciting the Buddha’s name, one transcends horizontally to ascend to the Precious Abode;
why need one seek the three chariots outside the gate?
The six thieves daily stir up turbulent waves; the treasures of the household are silently consumed without end.
Vowing to recite the Name with sincerity, the demonic hordes shall surely pay homage to the Buddha.

Turbid wisdom is difficult to purify; it is mostly due to indulging the senses and passions over many kalpas. If one hopes to bring an end to worldly entanglements in this very moment, there is only the diligent recitation of the Buddha’s name.

The mouth delights in summoning transgressions and is repeatedly exhorted; this arises solely because the Buddha’s name has not been recited often enough. From now on, keep count so that there is no interruption;
the ocean of karma will surely cease its boiling waves.
Fortunately, due to the subtle roots planted in past lives, I have today encountered this most excellent and extraordinary gateway.
Having merely obtained the guidance of the Compassionate Father of the Land of Bliss, I shall return to the source without needing to even snap my fingers.
Next, the twenty verses in the original rhyme by Dharma Master Miaoneng on the Pure Land: How marvelous!
This uniquely transcendent gate of easy practice Completely encompasses the sharp and dull faculties. By this, the supreme sages ascend to the Jewel Abode;
By this, ordinary beings restore their original mind.
My heart is grieved by long remaining within Jambudvīpa; bound internally and externally by māras, my nature has been rendered dull.
How fortunate that the World-Honored One extends his salvation, pointing westward so that I may soon depart from the east.
How can the virtue of the Western Teacher be fathomed? Even those bound by all fetters may find refuge in the palace of the seven treasures. Only after eons of cultivation does one attain this;
who could compare such supreme conditions to those found within the Land of Bliss?
To the west, there truly exists a pond of jeweled flowers; returning there will take no more time than a snap of the fingers. Hold fast to the Great Name with earnest devotion;
Amitābha will surely come to welcome you, as he knows it beforehand.
The West was originally the provisional within the real; apart from that, there is no more profound or subtle transmission. Pitiable are those who seek within the physical heart-mind;
at the moment of death, they find no master and are left in bewildered regret.
The wondrous existence of the West is itself true emptiness; only by understanding this can one know its extraordinary efficacy.
The six lands all conform to this principle, which is why the entire earth turns to it in reverence.
Whenever I contemplate the Pure Land, there are no seas or mountains; I feel deep shame for my attachment to the mundane world throughout many kalpas.
May I transcend this life to be reborn there, wandering day after day among the jeweled trees.
A single phrase of the Great Name contains manifold roots of goodness; the Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, together bestow their grace.
Even if sentient beings possess the sins of the hells, ten recitations can still move the sages to provide succor.
Holding the name of the wondrous Dharma is fundamentally without error; thus, one can fully encompass those of the highest capacity. Enlightenment does not depend on the power of investigative study;
those who seek something superior or distinct elsewhere are exceedingly rare.

My mind is heavily defiled; I am truly a fool. I know only to recite the name and bow before the Buddha’s image. Relying on Amitābha’s compassionate vow to gather us in, at the end of life, I shall surely go to the capital of the Awakened King.

For many lifetimes, one has harbored inverted views and grasped at the aggregates; wandering through the six realms of rebirth, one is beset by suffering. Now, fortunately, one holds the name that cuts across all dharmas;
one may freely ascend to the precious realm of the West.
The noble paths of the Three Vehicles generally involve long, winding rounds, relying entirely upon the habitual cultivation of many lifetimes.
Only the profound power of Amitābha’s vow allows one to rely solely on a single thought to entrust oneself to the womb of a lotus flower.

Ordinary people need not worry about being unable to be reborn; they should only fear harboring doubts regarding the name of that Buddha. If one can hold it single-mindedly as if remembering one's own mother, one will certainly be met by the Buddha in person at the moment of death.

How pitiable it is that in the past we were so deluded and mistaken; turning our backs on the broad highway, we hastened toward perilous paths. Who recognizes that the true mind is right before one’s eyes?
In a single phrase of Amitābha, its entire essence is fully revealed.
Do not doubt that the burden of karmic offenses has piled up like a slope; you must recite the name of the Buddha with a resolute mind.
If one were to compare this to those of the lowest grade in the Lotus Pond, who would have committed more evil deeds?

Although the gates of contemplation are supreme, they require great mental effort; how could inferior-minded ordinary beings easily understand them? How can they compare to the six characters of the Great Name?
By reciting them with single-minded devotion, one will surely reach the Lotus Pond.

If this black ox is to be swiftly tamed and made pure, it must rely upon the wheel of this person’s great vow. Only when its vast fame has been established for many tens of thousands of days will it first be fit to behold its compassionate parent in this lifetime.
Renunciation is difficult to encounter and the Dharma is difficult to hear; those who hear it should know that it is permeated by the Buddha’s virtue.
If one wishes not to render the power of his compassionate vow in vain, one must certainly transcend the worldly dust in this present life.
This realm is turbid and defiled, difficult to endure; a single point of numinous light is obstructed by dust.
Now, wishing to restore the mind to its original source, one must behold Amitābha before merit can be achieved.

Long detained in a foreign land, I have long been estranged from my kin. Alas! How bitter is this attachment to a body that is but a dream. Fortunately, I have received the message transmitted by the Teacher;
only now do I realize that the lotus has blossomed, just waiting for me.
Furthermore, following the original rhyme of "Master Miaoneng’s Verses on Feelings of Devotion toward the Pure Land," ten stanzas:
Holding the Name with diligence brings abundant roots of goodness; Transgressions and faults from beginningless time are all worn away. All Buddhas constantly protect and mind one because of this;
At the end of life, one will certainly behold Amitābha.
If one can merely recite the Buddha’s name once, boundless merit will be fully accomplished. Thus, he caused the tiger to open its mouth;
[the child] was born early amidst a lotus of the seven treasures.

If you wish and pray to reach the Jewel Pond in this very life, it depends entirely upon deep faith without contradiction. Furthermore, if you can hold the Buddha’s name until it becomes a continuous stream, you will surely attain the opening of a lotus on the highest branch.
First, one takes this defiled body to be permanent; thus one surely creates deep calamity and suffering that grows daily. All the sincere words of the Buddhas are for this very reason:
one must urgently give rise to revulsion and aspire to the Western Land.
The success of all teachings lies in a single mind; how could it tolerate even a momentary intrusion of deluded thoughts?

Only this method of holding the Name with faith and aspiration can cause the Sages to descend, even if one’s mind is largely distracted. (The *Guide to the Secret Treasury* states: "If one has deep faith and earnest aspiration for nianfo, yet the mind is frequently distracted during the practice, this constitutes the lowest grade of the lowest birth.

An ancient master said: 'Though the rank may be low, one dwells forever in non-retrogression; the joy within the lotus is superior to that in the celestial palaces. Thus, the poem by Beishan says: 'Provided one is reborn through transformation within the lotus, let it remain unopened for many kalpas. Within the lotus...")
Happiness equal to that of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven (unlike the human womb of parents).
Through the merit of pure aspiration, one achieves success in a single lifetime. At all times, never depart from the Great Name. Furthermore, one must maintain faith and vows with constant firmness;
only then can one proceed toward that realm at the moment of death.
It has been several thousand years since Śākyamuni entered parinirvāṇa; how lamentable that sentient beings are entangled by their karma! Fortunately, there is a single direct path:
if one pursues it every morning, one will surely be born within a lotus.
The self-nature is fundamentally pure; why should it be removed? Because it gives rise to greedy defilement, it must be eliminated. Therefore, one should make vows and uphold the Name;
only then can one sit upon the precious chariot in the future.
If you wish to purify your karmic offenses as soon as possible, you must recite the Buddha’s name with clarity and precision.
You should know that those who have already been born in the Pure Land did so one by one through a mind of diligent effort.

If hindrances are heavy, one should eliminate them through the practice of nianfo; yet even this is difficult to achieve without diligence. I have heard that even those who commit heinous crimes can board the precious chariot by relying on the strength of their hearts when they invoke the Name.

A single utterance of the Buddha’s name encompasses the three faculties. Even if the mouth recites while the mind is largely distracted, Every thought can still extinguish the source of suffering.
That Buddha especially pities those in this degenerate age; wherever his golden platform reaches, he receives the ordinary and the humble.
Now that I have fortunately encountered such a teaching, I shall by no means remain complacent or linger further in the East.

The Dharma-gate of the Pure Land is wondrous beyond measure; it perfectly gathers all classes of beings into the Lotus Palace. Even those for whom the signs of the fiery chariot appear can, by holding the Name, attain horizontal transcendence into the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

If you wish to be born in the precious lotus pond of the Land of Ultimate Bliss, worship the image and hold the name without neglecting the proper time. How many times each day will you prostrate, and how many tens of thousands of times will you recite the name?
Only then can one know in advance that one’s name shall be inscribed upon the petals of the flower.

Extensively studying the three vehicles is entirely provisional; upholding the name is the true single transmission. The Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, have praised it with earnestness;

All worldly affairs are entirely empty; only this practice of holding the name possesses supreme merit. By means of this, the broad tongue becomes universally pervasive, and all sages and saints of past and present offer their highest reverence.

Reciting the Buddha’s name amidst the clamor is superior to dwelling in the mountains; only when the environment is chaotic does one realize the weariness with this defiled world. Whether one's transgressions are few or many, let them not be considered;
rejoice in profound samādhi and enter among the lotus blossoms.

I vow to go to the Western Land, for this is my long-standing root of merit. Having received the Buddha’s profound kindness throughout many lifetimes, if I diligently recite his name even once, Amitābha will surely extend his own hand to rescue me.

Faith, aspiration, and the holding of the Name exhaust all errors; Perfectly integrated, direct, and swift, it easily accords with the capacity of beings. Its merit is supreme, requiring no concurrent study of other views;
Having read extensively through other schools, this Dharma is rare indeed.
Do not disdain counting recitations as the act of a fool; the progress of counting can be easily mapped.

quickly hold fast to the Buddha’s name and entrust yourself to a lotus womb.

A rosary of one hundred and eight beads rests in the hand; yet after a brief pause, it becomes covered in dust and grime. If one wishes for the flowers of the Pure Land to bloom early, one must begin to see their efficacy by counting the recitations and upholding the Name.
Morning after morning, I weep and lament for my aged parents, for they find it difficult to part from this body of burning affliction.
Having been tormented by a hundred sufferings for a long time, I pray that they may soon become inhabitants of the Land of Bliss.

Recite with mindfulness; with every sound, the golden-hued countenance is revealed.

"I shall deliver the multitudes solely by means of my Name."
The Name of Amitābha is a boundless vow; it universally gathers in the ordinary and the ignorant, sudden and complete.
Should even a rebellious evildoer turn their heart for but ten recitations, the fiery chariot of hell transforms into a purple-gold lotus.
Holding the name, one naturally attains the Great Name;
it resonates faintly as it is recited from the mouth. With hands counting the beads of the rosary, listen with profound stillness.

Provided one acts in this way without distraction, it will be as if the Buddha is truly present upon one's lips.

The name is uttered once; the Buddha is immediately revealed. (Chewu Chan Master said: "The name is established based on complete virtue; there is no name apart from virtue. Patriarch Shaokang reached the ultimate in this regard; thus, he was able to utter a single name and bring forth a single Buddha.
With every sound, the light of one's own mind is fully revealed. (That is, Chewu said: "One utterance of the Buddha’s name is one utterance of the mind.

It is clear right here—why wait to seek it? There is no need to repeatedly brandish the whip; the white ox has already drawn forth the ancient gold. For this reason, do not engage in miscellaneous contemplations; you simply need to be the person yourself.

The power of aspiration is strong (Master Jianmi said: "In every thought-moment of the six-syllable Great Name, joy and renunciation are fully present; this is precisely what is meant by the strength of the power of aspiration").
Holding the name is of great importance;
holding the name is of profound significance. One should investigate the Mahāyāna Sūtras of Perfect and Sudden Enlightenment: a single recitation in the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* makes one a Buddha;
ten breaths in the *Amitābha Sūtra* allow one to transcend rebirth.
The greatness of the name Hongming lies in its sound; thus, it can suddenly uproot the seeds of evil and rebellion.
It is easy to respond to and achieve through this, so let the eminent and wise not regard it as trivial.
Holding the name is like an echo;
when I recite the Buddha’s name, the resonance is like thunder. That Buddha hears it from afar and will surely come swiftly.

I call upon Amitābha with all my might; within the Lotus Pond assembly, I shall surely hear his voice.
Among them, there must be old kinsmen who will at last be willing to come early and deliver the good news.
Holding the name subdues delusion;
it is inappropriate to record the deluded mind. It is most appropriate to listen to the sound within one's own mouth. It is like the rising of thick clouds during the day;
one should take joy that the sunlight is not yet obscured.
Chanting the name subdues delusions and achieves wondrous merit; this merit issues from the mouth as a resonant sound.
It is like when a thousand monsters arise among men—a single clap of thunder can shatter the many malevolent minds.
When the three karmas are cultivated in their entirety, the oral recitation of the Buddha’s name must proceed from the mind; the manual manipulation of the prayer beads properly belongs to the body.
When the three karmas are cultivated in their entirety, the merit will surely be great; therefore, this may be widely circulated.

Reflect deeply upon the Buddha’s proclamation of the Tripiṭaka: there is nothing therein that does not serve as a warning to cultivate the three karmas. Therefore, he earnestly exhorts us to recite the name of Amitābha;
with every sound perfectly pure, one may easily transcend [saṃsāra].

Sincerely recite the Buddha’s name; sincerely recite Amitābha. The path back to the Lotus Land is direct. If for a moment you give rise to clever artifice, you will immediately fall into the realm of the heterodox.
Sincerely recite Amitābha; it is easy to leave behind the suffering of birth and death. If you crave wondrous and marvelous powers, it will be difficult to reach the place of cool serenity.
Sincerely recite the name of Amitābha; you must not let it cease from your lips. Let every sound be like weeping for a loved one, as you face directly west.
Sincerely recite the name of Amitābha; do not let the prayer beads fall from your hand. Holding them tens of thousands of times each day, your stay here will not last long.

Piercing my blood to vent my heart’s longing, I now pierce the blood of my tongue to reverently transcribe the *Amitābha Sūtra*. May all Buddhas respond with joy; Amitābha will surely rejoice even more.
As I now pierce the blood of my tongue and smear it across the Buddhas of the six directions, they will surely take pity on me together and cause me to be born in the Land of Bliss.
I pricked my left hand and drew blood to write out the Sixteen Vows; Amitābha desires to gather all universally, so there must surely be a portion for me.
I pricked my right hand and drew blood that flows back to the Nine Grades of the Pure Land; regardless of whether the lotuses are large or small, there must surely be one branch for me.

and your spiritual cultivation proceeds according to your wishes—this need not be divined to be known. (Ying) Since the Master’s commencement of the seven-day retreat, although the course of practice has increased slightly, alas, there is no one to provide the necessary vigilance.

Doubts arise repeatedly. Why is this? First, there is the doubt that after [your passing], there will be no succession of mature and seasoned statesmen to provide counsel; thus, I fear we may not succeed in our undertakings.

*Epigraph for "Following the Study of the Pure Land"*
I constantly sigh over the immeasurable sufferings of this Sahā world, where beings sink without fixed destination into the cycle of birth and death.

Having barely attained a human body, in a mere instant one follows evil retribution and descends into the dark underworld. How fortunate that the World-Honored One’s compassionate vow is profound; he has specially launched the vessel of mercy to rescue those submerged in suffering.
Without being asked, he spoke of the Dharma of holding the Name, desiring to lead all sentient beings out of the mundane dust. Thus was it propagated in the Eastern Land.

From our distant ancestors, countless high-minded practitioners who built huts on Mount Lu to cultivate the Pure Land have all attained rebirth there. Their descendants and various worthies have followed in their footsteps.

How tragic that the True Dharma has fallen into decline! Disciples are numerous, yet they delight in contending for cleverness. They merely recite the name of Amitābha until the mind becomes manifest;
yet, unwilling to accept this reality, they instead seek out "who" [is the Buddha]. It is like using a tile to knock at the door while striking one’s own mother. How lamentable!

Piteously, they gallop along the winding paths of the sheep-gut mountains; they delight only in the doctrine that "mind-only" exists and deny other lands. Such false views are all the more lamentable.
I pray that you, O Master, shall employ the power of your compassion and wisdom to apply the medicine of the Dharma everywhere to rescue those afflicted by the maladies of the age.

May every single word and phrase bring total coolness, enabling them to swiftly transcend the mundane realm without exception. Like a divine jewel containing immeasurable treasures, it is also like the celestial net reflecting infinite light.

A Thousand Radiances. How could the capacities of beings be divided into superior and inferior? Whatever portion one receives, it is all ultimately impermanent. (The *Shenzhu* is the collection of writings compiled by the Master;

it perfectly accords with the times to open up the perfect understanding. Students of Pure Practice should examine it closely. Alas, by what karmic affinity have I encountered this enlightened teacher? A single word has brought me relief, curing my blindness and folly.

(Ying formerly delighted in the practice of *nianfo*, yet he lacked essential guidance. The Dharma-treasure abides eternally in the world; may every person study it accordingly and receive its grace.
